title: Range of ideal multiplication on module stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $J,F$ sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\iota:J\to\mathcal O_X$ any linear morphism. Form $\mu:J\otimes F\to F$ as $\iota\otimes1$ followed by the left unitor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $x\in X$ let $S$ be the module stalk functor [def-pc-module-stalk-functor], with germs [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and let $e:S(\mathcal O_X)\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$ be a linear isomorphism sending every section germ to its ring germ. Put $I=\operatorname{range}(e\circ S(\iota))$. Then the range of $S(\operatorname{Im}(\mu)\hookrightarrow F)$ is $I\cdot F_x$, the submodule generated by $a m$ for $a\in I$, $m\in F_x$. No monomorphism hypothesis on $\iota$ is required.

source.place: Lemma 01CB (lemma-stalk-tensor-product), Section 17.3 and Lemma 01AG (lemma-abelian); combination used in coherent.tex, proof of Lemma 0CYV (lemma-systems-with-proper-support).

proof.text: Use the germ formula of the stalk-tensor isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-tensor]. Represent a pair of module germs on a common neighbourhood. The sectionwise tensor multiplication and the left unitor send a tensor of representatives to iota(a) times m. Naturality of stalk maps and the germ formula for e identify the stalk multiplication with a tensor m mapping to e(iota_x(a)) times m. For the categorical left unitor this formula follows from the monoidal unit identity for module sheafification and the triangle identity of its adjunction.

Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, so the multiplication range is contained in I times F_x. Conversely each generator r times m, with r=iota_x(a), is the image of the pure tensor a tensor m; the image is a submodule. Thus its range is I times F_x.

Stalk exactness identifies the stalk range of the abelian image inclusion with the range of the stalk multiplication [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact]. The canonical isomorphism from the abelian image to the chosen categorical image commutes with the inclusions. Its stalk is an isomorphism, hence does not change their ranges.
